explanation: A leader in Israel who helped rebuild the walls of Jerusalem and reform the Jewish community.
A holy place where Jews worshiped God and offered sacrifices; in Jerusalem, the temple was the center for religious activity.
An Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah and the rebuilding of Israel; he had unlawfully obtained a room in the temple.
Members of the tribe of Levi who had special religious duties, including service in the temple and teaching the people God's laws.
The seventh day of the week, a day of rest dedicated to God, where work was to cease and people were to focus on spiritual matters.
A tenth part of income or harvest given to the temple and priests to support their work and help the poor.
The rules and regulations that God gave his people through Moses and other prophets, including the Ten Commandments and many other instructions.
Being free from sin and impurity, both spiritual and physical, which was important for being able to worship God and participate in his service.
A holy covenant between a man and a woman, which in Nehemiah's time was complicated by mixed marriages with non-Jewish peoples.
